To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the exact time-variant and time-constant values of the central frequency of the linear response processes of SDOF and MDOF systems are the natural frequency of the undamped system and that the exact time-varying and stationary values of the bandwidth parameter of the linear response process of a SDOF system are equal to the square of the damping factor of the SDOF system and that the stationary value of the bandwidth parameter is zero for a non-classically dampled MDOF system

the central frequency and the bandwidth parameter of the SDOF and MDOF linear elastic systems subjected white noise excitation are time-varying and stationary random processes with the time-variant spectral moments and the stationary spectral moments, respectively.

the time-variant spectral characteristics of non-stationsary random processes, such as central frequency and bandwidth, are not only important quantities in describing the behavior of the processes but also useful quantities in analyzing the behavior of the linear structural response processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a unified theory and methodology for the computation and interpretation of spectral characteristics of general non-stationary complex-valued random processes, and their applications to linear structural systems subjected to white and general stationary non-stationary excitations.

the extension of the theory of spectral characteristics of non-stational random processes, and the application of this extension to the classical problem of determining the time-variant spectral characteristics of the response processes from linear structural models subjected to white noise excitations.

the development of a general theory for the spectral characteristics of non-stable non-stationary complex-valued random processes and the application of the developed theory to linear structural systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the time-variant behavior of the central frequencies and bandwidth parameters of the response processes is not a function of the system damping ratio, but is only a function of the initial conditions of the system.

the central frequency and the bandwidth parameter of the linear response processes of linear structural systems subjected to white-noise excitation are time-varying quantities that can be described by the exact closed-form expressions provided in this paper.
the central frequency of a real-valued non-statioanary random process is a time-dependent quantity that may increase or decrease with time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spectral characteristics of non-stationsry random processes are well-defined quantities that are useful for the analysis of linear structural models.
the time-variant spectral characteristics are not stationary random processes, and that the stationary spectral characteristics of these processes are not random processes.

the time-variant spectral characteristics of non-steady-state response processes of linear systems are completely determined by the initial conditions of the response processes and the spectral characteristics of the input processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the central frequency and the bandwidth parameter of the linear response processes of linear elastic systems subjected at rest to white noise exciation are both time-invariant and stationary, and their time-invariant values are equal to the natural frequency and the damping factor of the corresponding linear elastic system, respectively.

, in the case of white noise excitation, the central frequency and the bandwidth parameter of the linear response process of an SDOF or a MDOF linear elastic system can be expressed as functions of the spectral density function of the excitation process, the system parameters and the time.

, for linear elastic SDOF and both classically damped and non-classically (or non-classical) damped MDOF systems, the central frequency of their linear response processes is always time-invariant, whereas the bandwidth parameter is time-varying, but it converges to a constant value as time increases.
